findings.fix: Keep one selected signal (lime check only) and draw pad focus as a 2px --acc border. Raise the section labels to 16px tx-2 and the '+5% sp' values to 16px. Put a 1px --ui-line divider between the surface, weather and seed groups.

findings.where: kit tiles and pack row (my loadout, freebie kit, random kit, best kit, pack all, clear)
findings.what: Four tiles are the same size with the same weight, and only a lime left bar marks the selected one. Sub-lines at ~15px are dim. 'pack all' and 'clear' are bordered buttons at 20px, nearly as loud as the tiles. The 'burns on ascent' checkbox is a tiny orphan with unclear meaning.
findings.fix: Give the selected tile a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill, and let the others fall back to a --ui-line border. Set sub-lines to 16px tx-2. Make 'pack all' and 'clear' 16px text buttons. Group the data core row with a label, 'data core', and a 24px checkbox.

findings.what: The belt slots 1-0 are 32px with ~13px digits, and they sit far below the section label with a gap to the header. 'no armour equipped' is ~14px amber text. The warning sits tight against the ascend button (about 20px) and reads weak.
findings.fix: Make the belt slots 48px with 16px digits, and set 'belt' 16px. Raise the warning to 16px --warn with an 8px gap above the button. Align the belt row to the same left edge as the 'belt' label.

findings.where: header strip ('cold storage', 'ascending here', stats line)
findings.what: The 'ascending here' chip with its check duplicates the lime selected language, and it is unclear whether it is a button. The stats line ('420 x 340 m · 5 zones...') is ~18px tx-2, which is noise on a screen that already has a lot to read. The 'pre-raid' title (32px) is also close to the 'cold storage' size, so there are two competing headers.
findings.fix: Drop the check and make 'ascending here' plain 16px tx-2 text. Cut the stats line to '5 zones · 3 exits'. Make 'cold storage' 20px f-cond 600 so 'pre-raid' stays the single title.

findings.where: footer legend (esc close, click pick) and ascend keycap
findings.what: Legend text is ~16px tx-2 and the keycaps are ~13px. The legend is set at the card's left edge, with no divider tying it to the content. The 'enter' keycap in the lime button is tiny at ~14px and low-contrast. The legend does not clearly follow the live device.
findings.fix: Set keycap text to 16px with 8px padding, add a 1px --ui-line divider above the legend, and align it to the 24px content padding. Make the 'enter' keycap 16px in --acc-ink on a 1px --acc-ink border.

v.verdict: The card is clean and all lower case, but it is still a small list floating in a big empty card. Nothing shows focus, the title is not in a header row, and the amber on signed rows hides the lime accent.

findings.what: No row or button shows pad focus. 'signed' is outlined in amber, which reads as a state, not as focus. Last review's focus advice was not followed.
findings.fix: Fill the focused row with --ui-raised and add a 3px --acc left bar. Give the focused button an --acc fill with --acc-ink text. Keep idle buttons outlined in --ui-line-hi.

findings.where: title 'the terms' at (908-1012, 283) and the empty band above the list
findings.what: The title is centred and floats about 200px below the card top, with no header row. The X is alone in the corner. The list's left edge is x=261 and the title does not match it. The list ends at y=712, which leaves 300px dead at the bottom.
findings.fix: Put the title at the top left in a 56px header row, at x=261 and on the X's line, in 32px f-cond 700. Make rows 88px tall with 24px padding so the list fills the card. Anchor a 72px footer row at the bottom.

findings.what: The bonus is bold 32px-class condensed text, and every row has the same value. Unsigned rows are grey and signed rows are amber. Amber is the warning colour and sits next to the lime accent, and the grey fails as a hero number. Four equal heavy numbers weigh more than the row names.
findings.fix: Set the bonus to 20px f-cond 600. Use --tx-2 when idle and --acc when signed, with no amber. Keep the 32px weight for the title only.

findings.where: signed vs sign buttons at x=1533-1637
findings.what: The state is told apart only by a thin amber outline and amber text. The outline is 1px and low weight, so it fails the 'one primary action' rule and does not read from a couch.
findings.fix: Make 'signed' an --acc fill with --acc-ink text and a check glyph. Make 'sign' a --ui-line-hi outline in --tx-1. Use 48px high buttons, 120px wide.

findings.what: The descriptions are about 14px and dim, below the 16px floor. They are explaining sentences, and the longest one runs 'about 356 seconds instead of 540'.
findings.fix: Raise them to 16px --tx-2 with at least 4.5:1 contrast. Shorten each to a few words, for example 'raid clock -33%'.

findings.where: 'sp x1.10' at (261,733) and the divider at y=756
findings.what: The total is a tiny amber 14px label under the list, as a stray line. The divider and 'sign nothing' sit close to it at uneven gaps of about 20px and 12px.
findings.fix: Put 'sp x1.10' in the 72px footer row at 20px --acc on the right. Put 'sign nothing' at the left of the same row. Use 24px between the list and the footer.

findings.what: The X has a hard bright 1px border and a heavy glyph. It is brighter than the content, and it sits 8px off the card's corner padding while the list is inset 164px.
findings.fix: Use --ui-line-hi for the border and 24px inset. Highlight it only when focused.

findings.what: The list panel is the same colour as the card, so only a 1px line separates them. Rows have no padding rhythm: text sits close to the top at 8px.
findings.fix: Fill the list with --ui-panel against a --ui-bg card. Use 24px horizontal and 16px vertical row padding, and --ui-line dividers.

v.verdict: It is a clean, readable result card with a clear lime primary action. But it holds too much for one screen, the stats are inconsistent (kills appears twice), the small text is below the guide's size floor, and the amber and teal blocks compete with the lime button.

findings.where: Whole card, below the two total boxes
findings.what: Too many stacked elements for one result screen. It has two score panels, a lone gem tile, a 5-tile stat strip, three medals, an xp line, an extract-carrying line, a feedback button and the leaderboard button, all in one narrow column. Nothing is grouped, and the vertical rhythm is uneven: the gaps run about 8px, 16px and 40px.
findings.fix: Cut it to hero, two panels, one medal row and the primary action. Move the stat strip and the feedback toggle off this screen, or fold them into the panels. Use 16px gaps between groups and 24px between sections.

findings.what: There are two hero numbers at about 28px each, so the guide's one 56px hero per screen is missing. They are in amber and teal, which fight the lime button for attention. Amber also reads as P1 and as warn, and it is used here for score and for the personal-best chip.
findings.fix: Make the score total a single 56px f-cond 800 hero in tx-1 or lime. Drop the money total to the 20px body size in tx-1. Keep amber for the 3px rarity bar only.

findings.what: A single 62px icon tile with a blue underline has no label and no meaning. It floats between the panels and the stat strip and looks like a leftover or a broken slot.
findings.fix: Label it, or move it into the money panel as an item row, or delete it.

findings.where: Stat strip: kills, accuracy, containers, time, health
findings.what: The strip is redundant with the panel above, which already shows kills. Its labels are about 11px, below the 16px label floor and the 14px fine size. The same small size is used for the medal captions ('first out', 'untouched', 'ghost'), the 'personal best' chip and the panel headers.
findings.fix: Use 16px labels with +.04em tracking and 28px values. Drop the duplicate kills tile. Show 3 tiles at most.

findings.where: Two panels, row text and dividers
findings.what: The row labels in the panels are bold white and set in tracked small caps-style spacing. The values are coloured and the same weight as the labels, so every row has equal weight. The two orange and teal underline dividers are 1px and barely visible. The '+1,000 sp' and '+$2,000' bonus rows get no more emphasis than the base rows.
findings.fix: Make labels tx-2 at 16px weight 600. Make values tx-1 at 20px weight 700. Use a --ui-line divider.

findings.where: Secondary text: '+148 xp', 'extract carrying 1x data core', subtitle 'out clean · never spotted'
findings.what: These three lines are muted grey, about 15px, centred and floating with no container. They read as filler, and the subtitle is an explaining sentence, which the brief counts as a defect. The checkmark is the only green on the card.
findings.fix: Remove the subtitle. Put xp in the score panel as one row. Merge the carrying line into the money panel's items row.

findings.what: The x is a 48px boxed button at the card corner, and it sits outside the title's centre axis, so the header is unbalanced. The title 'extracted' is teal at about 28px, under the 32px title size, and the teal also appears in the money panel.
findings.fix: Make the title 32px. Inset the x 16px from the card edge. Keep teal for the title only.

findings.where: Feedback button 'how did that run feel +' and the leaderboard button
findings.what: The idle-state feedback button has a thin border and grey text, and it sits 30px above a wide lime fill button. The 240px-wide lime button is the only primary action, which is right, but it is dark-ink condensed text at about 20px with no focus ring and no key hint, so you cannot tell where the pad focus is.
findings.fix: Give the primary button a visible 2px focus outline in white or lime with 4px offset. Add a key hint at 16px. Make the feedback control a text link at 16px.

v.verdict: The card is tidy and the lime leaderboard button reads as the main action, but it holds too many stacked elements, the stats contradict the score, the type is tiny, and the amber, teal, gold and lime colours compete.

findings.where: stat chips row (kills 0, accuracy 0%, containers 0, time 0:00, health 100)
findings.what: The chips read 0 kills and 0:00 time directly under a panel that shows 700 sp from kills. This looks like a data bug or a placeholder row, it duplicates the kills line, and it adds clutter.
findings.fix: Remove the row, or fix the values. If it stays, drop the duplicate kills chip and use real values at 20px for the number and 16px for the label.

findings.what: There are two hero totals (2,000 sp in amber and $2,520 in teal) at about 28px, plus a 32px title and a bright lime button. The guide's 56px hero size is not used, so the eye bounces between five competing points.
findings.fix: Make the 2,000 sp total the single hero at 56px, f-cond 800. Drop $2,520 to 32px in tx-1. Keep the title at 32px.

findings.where: labels and captions: stat chip labels, medal names, 'out clean · never spotted', 'personal best', +148 xp
findings.what: These render at about 10 to 13px, below the 16px floor in the guide. The chip labels and medal names are unreadable from a couch. The xp line is dim grey and floats alone.
findings.fix: Set every label to 16px minimum, 600 weight. Use tx-1 for the xp line at 20px. Delete the 'out clean · never spotted' explaining sentence.

findings.where: colour use: amber score panel, teal money panel, gold medals, lime button
findings.what: Four saturated hues sit in one small card. Teal is reserved for extraction. Amber and gold sit next to the lime button, and the guide says they must not be placed side by side. The amber and teal borders and the teal money values add noise without meaning.
findings.fix: Make both panels --ui-panel with a --ui-line-hi border. Use tx-1 for the values, with lime only on the hero total. Keep teal only on the 'extracted' title. Use a 3px rarity-gold bar on the medals, with no fill.

findings.where: vertical rhythm, between the gem tile, stat chips, medals, xp, feedback button and leaderboard
findings.what: Spacing is uneven. Gaps vary from about 8 to 40px, and the lone gem tile has no label or purpose. The card holds seven stacked groups and has dead space beside the narrow content column.
findings.fix: Remove the unlabelled gem tile or give it a name. Put gaps on the 8px grid at 24px between groups. Make the content column the full card width minus 48px padding.

findings.what: This is a low-contrast grey outlined button about 40px tall, sitting directly above the primary button. It is a second ask on a results screen, and the '+' is cryptic.
findings.fix: Move it to a 16px text link in the footer, or remove it. If it stays as a button, give it a 48px height and tx-1 text.

findings.where: row dividers and values in the score panel ('extraction x2 +1,000 sp' underline)
findings.what: One row has a coloured underline while the others have none, and the values are bold amber at the same weight as the labels. The panel looks like a template.
findings.fix: Use a 1px --ui-line divider between all rows. Set labels in tx-2 at 16px and values in tx-1 at 20px, weight 700. Use a 24px row height.

findings.where: close x at top right vs. the leaderboard button
findings.what: The card has both an x close and a separate leaderboard button. The x is a 48px outlined square, and its focus state is not visible. The close sits far from the centred title, which leaves the header unbalanced.
findings.fix: Give the x a 2px lime focus ring and align it with the 32px title baseline at 24px from the card edge. Mark the leaderboard button as the default pad focus.

v.verdict: The ascend button is a strong primary action and the card structure is sound, but the dead column, unreadable map labels and tiny, inconsistent type keep it at a 3.

findings.where: right column, y 530-890 (between the belt and the armour warning)
findings.what: About 360px of empty panel sits between the belt and the warning. The previous advice to fill or collapse it was not followed. The column reads as unfinished, and the belt keys at 30px are tiny.
findings.fix: Add a 4-column grid of 72px pack slots (--ui-raised fill, 1px --ui-line border) under the pack header. Otherwise move the belt and the warning up under the data core row with 24px gaps. Put 1px --ui-line dividers between kit, pack and belt. Enlarge the belt cells to 48px.

findings.where: map labels ('the long dock', 'foreman office', 'blast freezer', 'chill row', 'exit a/b/c')
findings.what: The labels sit on top of room boxes ('the long dock' crosses a box edge, 'blast freezer' overlaps the grid and the purple square). The exit labels touch their markers. Label sizes vary and the white text has no clean contrast on the blue fills. The purple dashed squares have no legend.
findings.fix: Set every label to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 with a 1px --ui-void halo. Move labels at least 8px clear of boxes and markers. Set exit labels in --extract at 16px. Remove the purple squares or add a 'keyed' legend entry. Draw room boxes with a --ui-raised fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: 'blackout +5% sp' wraps onto 2 lines, which breaks the row rhythm and height. Night is both selected and focused, so it has a lime check, a lime border and a bright outline at once, which looks heavy. The section labels ('conditions', 'surface', 'weather', 'seed') are about 14px and dim, and 'conditions' vs 'surface' is a double heading.
findings.fix: Widen the column by 20px, or drop the value to a right-aligned 16px 'sp +5%' so every row stays on one line. Draw selected as a lime check plus a --ui-raised fill, and focus as a single 2px --acc border. Remove the 'conditions' heading. Set the section labels to 16px tx-2 with 16px of space above them.

findings.where: type sizes across the card (kit sublines, 'no armour equipped', 'burn for intel', 'enter', footer legend)
findings.what: Many strings are about 13-14px, below the 16px floor, and the warning is tiny amber text. The hierarchy is also flat on the right: 'kit', 'pack' and 'belt' are small bold labels with the same weight as the row text, and 'no data core' is centred and grey with no clear alignment.
findings.fix: Set the sublines, warning and checkbox label to 16px. Set the 'kit', 'pack' and 'belt' section labels to 16px f-cond 700 tx-2 with a 1px divider above each. Left-align 'no data core' to the icon. Set the warning to 16px --warn.

findings.where: kit tiles (my loadout, freebie kit, random kit, best kit)
findings.what: Selection is shown by a lime check and a thin left bar, while the other tiles are close in tone, so the selected state is weak. The tiles are only about 52px tall and 16px apart, which feels cramped next to the large ascend button.
findings.fix: Give the selected tile a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill, and use a --ui-line border on the others. Increase the tile height to 64px with an 8px gap.

findings.what: The blue wash fill competes with the dark UI palette and is not a token colour. The map takes about 55% of the card while the right column is starved.
findings.fix: Fill the map with --ui-void and draw rooms with a --ui-raised fill. Keep teal for the exits only. Shrink the map by about 10% and give the space to the right column.

findings.where: header and card bottom (title, header row, footer)
findings.what: The footer row ('esc close', 'click pick') is small and floats beside a large empty bar. The map header shows two title-like items ('cold storage' at 24px and 'pre-raid' at 32px), so there are two competing titles. The 'ascending here' chip duplicates the meaning of the selected state.
findings.fix: Keep 'pre-raid' as the only 32px title. Set 'cold storage' to 20px tx-1. Remove the 'ascending here' chip, or turn it into plain 16px tx-2 text. Set the footer legend to 16px.

findings.what: The buttons are about 36px tall with 14px text. The checkbox is an empty 32px box with a dim border and has no clear checked state. Both look disconnected from the data core icon.
findings.fix: Make the buttons 40px tall with 16px text and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Draw the checkbox at 24px with a 2px --ui-line-hi border and a lime fill when on. Put the icon, 'data core' and the checkbox on one row with 16px spacing.

v.verdict: The earlier advice was mostly followed: the title now sits at the top left, the focused row has a lime bar, and signed is a lime fill. The card still looks half-built, because the list ends at y=648 and about 370px of the card is empty below it.

findings.what: The content stops at 'sign nothing' (y=777) and leaves a dead band of about 250px at the bottom of the card. The content column (x=261-1659) is also off-centre against a card that spans x=97-1822, and the X sits outside it. The screen looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Make the rows 100px tall so the list fills y=200-760. Pin a 72px footer at the bottom of the card with 'sign nothing' on the left and the 'sp x1.10' total on the right. Use a 48px side margin so the column spans x=145-1775 and lines up with the X.

findings.what: The descriptions are about 14px in --tx-2, and some are long ('40% more machines, pillagers and criers.'). They are below the 16px floor and read as explaining sentences. The sentence-ending period and the 'raid clock -33%: 356s' colon make them look cluttered.
findings.fix: Set them to 16px --tx-2 with a minimum 4.5:1 contrast. Cut each to 4 words or fewer, for example 'machines +40%' and 'raid clock -33%'. Remove the trailing period and the colon.

findings.what: The idle 'sign' buttons are 48px high with a thin outline and a small 16px label. At 1080 from a couch they barely read as buttons next to the lime 'signed' fills. The focused 'signed' button has a double outline (lime fill, dark ring, lime ring) that looks like a rendering glitch.
findings.fix: Use a 2px --ui-line-hi border on idle buttons and 18px label text in --tx-1. Replace the double ring on the focused button with a single 3px --acc-hover outline offset 2px.

findings.what: The bonus text is lime on signed rows and grey on idle rows, so lime appears three times per row (bar, text, fill). The same '+5% sp' value is repeated on all five rows and carries no information.
findings.fix: Keep the signed bonus in --tx-1 and the idle bonus in --tx-2. Reserve lime for the button fill and the focus bar. Show the +5% once in the header ('each term +5% sp') or only on the active rows.

findings.what: The total is the hero number but is drawn at about 18px in lime, squeezed under the list with a hairline below it. It is the screen's key result, yet it is smaller than the row titles.
findings.fix: Draw it at the 56px hero size in f-cond 800, right-aligned in the footer row, with a 16px --tx-2 label 'score bonus' above it. Remove the hairline at y=711.

findings.what: The title measures about 28px, below the 32px token, and the rule at y=177 is dim. The title's left edge (x=261) does not line up with the X (x=1759-1807), which sits 50px higher and outside the column.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 and centre it vertically on the X (y=91). Add a 56px header row with the rule at y=112 spanning the full card width.

findings.what: The list has a 1px light outer border plus row dividers, and it gets a visible left bar only on the focused row. The first row also shows a double top edge (y=203-206). The panel reads as a template table.
findings.fix: Remove the outer border and keep only the --ui-line dividers between rows. Fill alternating rows with --ui-panel and --ui-raised only for the focused row, so the focus bar is the only accent.

v.verdict: This is a clean, correctly lower-case scoreboard card with a clear title and live prompt, but the empty state is dead space, the card is small, and the dim backdrop still competes with it.

findings.what: The empty state is a lone 20px 'no scores yet' line on a 150px band of nothing. The card looks unfinished and the content has no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Centre the empty state in the body. Use 20px tx-2 with a 16px tx-2 hint, or collapse the card to about 180px tall. Alternatively show 3 ghost rows (1px --ui-line, 40% opacity) so the layout previews the filled list.

findings.what: The lobby behind the card is only blurred and dimmed. Bright character sprites and the teal and purple pad rings sit right next to the card edge (the figure at x1250 y350 overlaps it), so the modal does not separate cleanly.
findings.fix: Use the guide's --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) plus a 6px blur. Reduce the sprites and rings to about 40% brightness behind the card.

findings.what: The x is a 48px boxed button that duplicates 'press any key'. On a walk-up screen two controls compete and the x is the heavier of the two. The 1px --ui-line-hi box is visually louder than the title.
findings.fix: Remove the boxed x on this walk-up card and keep the live prompt as the only action. If the x stays for consistency with other windows, shrink it to 32px with no border (glyph only, tx-2) at 16px from the corner.

findings.what: The lime ring with a dot plus 'press any key' at about 22px is the correct primary action, but the dot reads as a radio button or toggle. The 20px text sits tight to the right padding, and the prompt does not name the device key or pad button.
findings.fix: Replace the radio with the actual key glyph (a 24px keycap, or the pad button for pad users). Keep the text at 20px 600 tx-1 and the 32px bottom padding.

findings.what: The 36px lime tab on the top edge is too small and offset to read as a deliberate accent. It looks like a clipping artefact.
findings.fix: Make it a 3px bar, 64px wide, aligned flush to the x713 text edge, or drop it.

findings.what: The chip is tiny (about 12px) and dark green on dark, so it fails the 16px minimum and the contrast floor. It also sits in the scrim as stray clutter.
findings.fix: Set it to 16px tx-2 on a --ui-panel pill with 8px padding, or remove it from this screen.

findings.what: The wordmark floats over the busy blurred scene with no panel, and it is roughly title size, so it competes with the card title. It is also offset from the card's 713px text edge.
findings.fix: Dim it to tx-2 at 20px, or hide it behind the modal. Keep it at the 5% margin (x96) only if it is the same size on every walk-up screen.

findings.what: At 558x255 the card is far from the guide's 90 percent centred card. The title, empty line and prompt are loosely spaced with a thin 1px divider that barely shows.
findings.fix: Keep it compact as a walk-up toast, but use consistent 32px padding. Set the title at y+32, the body at +56, and the footer row at 72px tall with the divider at --ui-line-hi.

v.verdict: This is a clean, calm player 2 title screen with a clear lime primary action, but the orange gradient wordmark fights the lime button, the type is small, and the content is a narrow cluster lost in a big empty frame.

findings.where: wordmark 'pillagers' (x 800-1120, y 360-442) and the 'enter the undercroft' button (x 681-1239, y 511-567)
findings.what: The title is a saturated orange-amber gradient with a drop shadow, and the lime button sits right under it. Two hot colours of near-equal weight compete, and amber is meant for P1 on this P2 screen. The title is bold and so is the main action, which breaks the rule of boldness in one place. The gradient is also a template tell.
findings.fix: Make the wordmark flat --tx-1 at 72px, f-cond 800, with no gradient or shadow, so the lime button is the only hot element. Or keep a single flat cyan underline in the P2 colour. Delete the amber on this screen.

findings.what: The whole menu is a 558px column in the middle of 1920 and the screen is otherwise empty black. There is no backdrop art, no hero image and no sense of place. The only identity is the wordmark, so it reads as a generic template and not as ARC Raiders or Halo Reach.
findings.fix: Put a dimmed key-art or raid scene behind a 40% --scrim. Left-align the menu column at x 96, or add a vertical rule and a side panel for save details. Place the title block at y 280 and the actions at y 520.

findings.what: The save row is 16px light body text. The detail '0 raids · $900 · 0 xp' is thin grey and low contrast at couch distance. The selected state is only a 1px lime outline plus lime text, with no fill. 'saves' is a faint orphan label. The row is the same height as the input row below, so there is no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Make the row 64px tall with --ui-raised fill and a 4px lime bar on the left. Set the name at 20px 600 --tx-1 and the stats at 16px --tx-2. Set 'saves' at 16px 600 +.04em --tx-2. Keep the 24px gap above the row and use a 16px gap between rows.

findings.what: A teal outlined chip sits alone at top centre. Teal is reserved for extraction. The chip has no clear meaning and no relation to the top-right buttons, so it is stray clutter. It also uses a different radius and border colour from the other chips.
findings.fix: Fold it into the bottom legend, or put it left of 'go fullscreen' at x 1400, y 32. Use --ui-line-hi, --tx-2, 16px and 4px radius, and drop the teal.

findings.what: A 14px muted label sits under the primary button and is not clearly tied to either. It reads as an afterthought, and its role (a player tag) is ambiguous. It needs to say that this is P2 and which key or button continues.
findings.fix: Make it a 16px cyan-tinted pill, 'player 2', 24px above the wordmark at y 330. Put the live key prompt on the button, e.g. 'enter the undercroft · [enter]'.

findings.what: The name field and the two buttons are equal in weight and tiny, at 16px bold with 40px height. The field looks like a button. 'change name' and 'create a new save' are secondary actions that clutter the primary path. The row does not align to a clear grid and its gaps are 8px against 24px elsewhere.
findings.fix: Make it 48px tall. Give the field a 1px --ui-line border and a --ui-bg fill, and give the buttons ghost style. Collapse 'change name' into an edit icon in the save row, and set the row 24px under the save row.

findings.where: bottom legend (x 726-1194, y 1030-1056) and version stamp (x 97-243, y 1040-1055)
findings.what: The key legend at 16px and the version stamp at about 13px are both dim and small. The version is under 14px, below the floor. The legend (wasd, mouse, lmb, e, f1) is gameplay help on a title screen, which is clutter. The stamp is inset at x 97 while the top-right buttons sit at x 1823, so the margins are inconsistent.
findings.fix: Drop the legend from the title screen, since f1 controls covers it. Set the version at 14px --tx-2, x 96, y 1032, and mirror the 96px margin on the right.

findings.what: The tagline is a 20px muted line that is cramped 24px under the wordmark and 24px above the button, with letter-spaced punctuation. It looks like filler, and it is not the quiet role the type scale gives it.
findings.fix: Set it at 16px 600 +.08em --tx-2. Space it 16px under the wordmark and 40px above the button, so the title block separates from the action block.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the one I reviewed before, a yes/no prompt over a live raid. The lime yes button is clear and the card is clean, but the card overlaps the HUD and has dead space and weak yes/no styling.

findings.what: The card sits flush against the team score and extract chips. It covers the top of the extract pill and cuts the raid HUD. It is also off-centre vertically (centre y420 against 540), and the backdrop is not dimmed, so the live raid at full brightness competes with the question.
findings.fix: Centre the card at y540 (y375-705). Add a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer behind it, with an optional 4px blur, so the HUD and map drop to about 40% brightness.

findings.what: The question is 32px but sits in a 170px-tall band of dead space above the buttons. The '11' countdown at top-right is 20px, with no label and no ring, so it reads as a stray number. The title and the countdown do not share a baseline.
findings.fix: Reduce the title-to-button gap to 32px. Turn the countdown into a 16px tx-2 '11s' aligned to the title baseline, or a thin 3px lime bar that drains along the card top edge.

findings.what: The yes button is a 405x100 lime slab, and the no button is a hairline outline that is hard to see (border near --ui-line). The pair is lopsided, and no focus state is shown on 'no'. The lime fill is also much heavier than the title, which breaks the rule of boldness in one place per screen.
findings.fix: Make both buttons 64px tall. Keep yes as the lime fill. Give no a 1px --ui-line-hi border with tx-1 text, so it is clearly a button. Add a 2px lime focus ring when no is selected. Keep the 32px gap between the buttons.

findings.what: The 'y yes' and 'n no' labels use a bare key letter, so they read as a typo. The labels are also only 24px against a 100px button.
findings.fix: Put the key in a 28px keycap (1px border, 16px text) beside the 20px 600 'yes' label. On pad, swap the keycap for the pad button glyph.

findings.what: A short lime tick sits on the top-left, offset from the x539 text edge. It looks like a clipped progress bar and aligns with nothing.
findings.fix: Either make it a full-width 3px timer bar, or align it to the x539 content edge at 64px wide.

findings.what: The HUD is crowded. The goals box, team score, extract pill, 'player 2 joined' toast, notice strip and f1 chip are all visible at once, and this modal is stacked on top. The 'cache' label in purple and the 'player 2 joined' toast overlap the weapon slot area.
findings.fix: While the modal is open, hide the toast and the goals box. Dim the HUD under the scrim. Move the 'cache' label 8px clear of the slot edge.

findings.what: The padding is uneven: 47px left and right, 46px below the buttons, but the top has about 54px above the title, and the card is 935px wide for two short items. The card feels like a generic wide template.
findings.fix: Narrow the card to about 720px with 32px padding on all sides, and keep the title at 32px 700.

v.verdict: This frame is a raid screenshot with a 'want easy mode?' modal, not the player 2 title I reviewed before, and the modal is a flat black box with a glaring lime fill that has no hierarchy or craft behind it.

findings.what: The image is not the p2-1080 title screen. It shows the in-raid HUD with a modal over it, so my earlier advice on the wordmark, save row and 'player 2 window' pill can't be checked and none of it appears to have been done.
findings.fix: Re-capture the real p2 title screen. If this modal is meant to be the p2 screen, say so, and give it the title composition from my earlier review.

findings.what: The card is an unframed flat black rectangle with no border, radius or scrim. The raid HUD (score, timer, goals) runs at full brightness around it, so the modal fights the clock and team score directly above it. The card also sits off-centre (centre y 420 against a 540 screen centre) and butts against the 'extract 140m' chip at y 260. The lime sliver at x 493-562 on its top edge looks like a glitch.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use --ui-panel fill on an 80% --scrim over the whole screen. Centre the card at y 540 and make it 880x360. Make the top edge either a full-width 4px lime bar or nothing.

findings.what: The 406x101 solid lime block is the loudest element on the screen, bigger than the title and the hero numbers. It is a Fortnite-style CTA with no bounce or inner structure. The 20px 'y yes' label is dark text centred in a huge field. On a screen that asks about easy mode it also pushes the player toward 'yes'.
findings.fix: Cut the button to 64px tall. Use 24px f-cond 700 text in --acc-ink and put the 'y' key hint in a 28x28 chip at the left. Keep it as the only lime fill. Decide the default deliberately, since lime should mean 'selected'.

findings.what: The no button is a near-invisible 1px outline on black, with white text at about 20px. It reads as disabled, and with no focus state shown, a pad player can't tell which button is active. Its contrast with the card is below the --ui-line-hi spec.
findings.fix: Fill it --ui-raised with a 2px --ui-line-hi border and --tx-1 label. Show a 3px lime focus outline on whichever button holds pad focus. Use the same 64px height as the yes button.

findings.what: The title is about 32px but sits cramped in the top-left, with 12px of dead space beside it. The countdown '12' at x 1370, y 346 is tiny, grey and unlabelled, so the player can't tell what it counts down. The card has a 100px empty band between the title row and the buttons. The title also reads as a question with no context about what easy mode changes.
findings.fix: Set the title at 32px f-cond 700 --tx-1, with a 16px --tx-2 line below it that states the effect in 6 words or fewer. Make the countdown a 40px hero-style number in a 56px ring or bar, tinted --tx-2. Cut the gap to 32px between the title block and the buttons.

findings.what: The chip has a green-tinted fill with a bold monospace-looking face. It is tight against the screen edge, at x 4 where the margin should be 5%. It matches no other chip style, such as the 'f1 controls' chip or the 'in pillager's party' tooltip.
findings.fix: Use a 16px f-cond 600 --tx-2 label on a --ui-panel pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Move it to x 96, y 32, or fold it into the footer legend.

findings.where: HUD mixed type and panels (goals x 1603-1900; team score x 795-1125; support mg x 1606-1910)
findings.what: The three panels use different paddings, radii and type. The goals panel has no title divider, and its rows are in a tight 26px stack at about 20px. Team score mixes a 36px hero '210 sp' with 'you 105 sp' and 'p1 105 sp' in a cramped right column that touches the panel edge. The 'support mg' panel has a 60px ammo hero. There are about 4 different panel border treatments, and the text sizes (14, 18, 20, 36, 60) don't follow the 5-step scale.
findings.fix: Apply --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line and 4px radius, with 16px padding, to all three. Limit sizes to 56, 32, 20 and 16. Put 'you' and 'p1' on separate 16px --tx-2 lines, with 16px padding between them and the panel edge.

findings.what: Four different treatments crowd the corner: orange-outline circle icons, yellow-text 'concealed', teal-text 'in cover' and the 'f1 controls' chip. The bars use a different font weight and no panel behind the text. The armour bar's label sits on a light-blue fill at low contrast, and the hp bar is 8px from the screen edge. The yellow 'concealed' text and orange text read as an accent competing with lime.
findings.fix: Make the two status tags one 16px chip style in --tx-1 on --ui-panel. Give the bar labels --acc-ink or --tx-1 text on a darkened fill. Set both bars to 360x24 with 8px between them, and move the corner to x 96, y 960.

v.verdict: the raid hud is readable and mostly lower case, but the top-centre is a stack of five boxes that crowd each other and the 'final rush' alert, and the bottom-left hud has uneven widths and weak contrast.

findings.where: top-centre stack (timer, team score, extract chip, final rush banner)
findings.what: Four separate dark boxes of different widths sit in one column and nearly touch. The score box bottom edge (y≈214) runs into the extract chip (y≈226). The final rush banner overlaps the player 2 marker and the extract arrow. There's no clear spacing rhythm and no single hero. The timer, 'team score 210 sp' and the red alert all compete at similar weight.
findings.fix: Leave a 16px gap between all boxes and centre them on the same width. Make the timer the only 56px hero. Drop 'team score' to 20px with you/p2 in 16px muted text. Move the final rush banner to y≈260 with 24px of clear space around it, and move the extract chip into the timer row or beside it.

findings.what: The alert is the most important message, but it is a small 270px box with a thin red left bar. The warning triangle and title are about 32px, so it reads weaker than the timer. 'kills x1.05 sp' is 20px white on dark red, which is flat and cramped, with about 8px of padding.
findings.fix: Widen it to about 420px with 16px padding. Use a 32px title in --danger and a 20px tx-2 subline. Keep the triangle at 32px. Add a 4px --danger left bar and fill it with --ui-panel at 90% so it reads as the one hot element.

findings.where: extract chip and player 2 world label
findings.what: The 'extract 140m' teal chip is jammed between the score panel and the final rush banner. The teal triangle arrow and the 'player 2' world tag are clipped under the banner at (990,298). The 'player 2' tag is also blue on brown at 12px, which fails the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Move the extract chip and its arrow out of the banner's footprint, for example to the left of the timer at y=60 with 16px gap. Raise the world tag to 16px with a --ui-panel plate. Keep player 2 cyan, as the style guide says.

findings.what: The armour bar is 405px wide and the hp bar is roughly the same width. Their labels are crammed in as 'armour 60' and 'hp 100', and the hp text is oversized next to the armour text. The 'f1 controls' chip floats at x≈410, not aligned to the bars' left edge (x=24). The lime and green fills on brown and purple terrain give weak contrast, and the white label on light blue is low contrast.
findings.fix: Use one 16px label and one 20px value format for both bars. Make both bars 32px high and the same width. Put the labels on a dark plate with 4.5:1 contrast. Align the f1 chip's left edge to x=48 (5% margin) on its own row above the bars.

findings.where: bottom-right ammo panel and weapon slots
findings.what: The 'support mg 60 / 360' panel uses a 56px hero, which is fine. But its right edge touches the screen (1910px) with no 5% margin. The weapon slot row is bottom-centre, and number keys 3,4,6,7,8,9,0 float as stray digits over the terrain with no slot boxes. Empty slots look like leftover debug text.
findings.fix: Inset the ammo panel 48px from the right and bottom edges. Draw 8 equal 64px slot tiles with a --ui-line border for all slots, and show the numbers inside the tiles. Dim the empty ones to 40% opacity.

findings.where: left feed message '2 minutes left · nearest extraction 140m west.'
findings.what: It is a full sentence with a trailing period, and it repeats the extract chip's 140m. That is the explaining-sentence clutter the brief bans, and it sits on a bright patch of ground with an amber left bar. The 'player 2 joined' toast at bottom-centre is a third separate box in another style.
findings.fix: Cut to '2 minutes left' and delete the distance (it is already in the chip). Put it and 'player 2 joined' in the same left feed list, with one consistent 16px style, a 4px accent bar and a --ui-panel fill.

findings.what: The goals dropdown is a lighter, wider box with a chevron and a different corner radius from the other panels. The 'keyboard' chip in the top-left is 14px, in green text, and a different style again. The whole HUD mixes at least four panel treatments.
findings.fix: Use one panel style: --ui-panel at 90%, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 8px/16px padding. Match the goals box to it and move 'keyboard' to the footer legend at 14px tx-2 with no green.

findings.where: player 2 tag in the top-left, 'meridian strongbox' label
findings.what: The player 2 plate at the left is a small 150px box with a thin bar in cyan and green. It has no hp number and its blue name is hard to read on the brown ground. The 'meridian strongbox' label in amber on brown at 20px has weak contrast and no plate.
findings.fix: Give both a --ui-panel plate with 8px padding. Make the player 2 name 16px tx-1 with a cyan 3px bar, and use warn amber on the plate for the strongbox label.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has the right pieces, but the top centre is a stack of five competing boxes, and the weapon slots, bars and goals dropdown do not share one style.

findings.where: top centre: timer, rain icon, team score, extract chip and final rush banner
findings.what: Five boxes are stacked in a column and overlap. The team score panel sits directly on the timer's bottom edge and the extract chip. The banner crowds the chip and cuts into the compass arrow. The eye has no single first read. The timer, the score and the red banner all compete, and nothing sets the 56px hero apart.
findings.fix: Keep the timer as the one hero element (56px, f-cond 800). Move the team score to a smaller 20px row under it with 16px gaps. Move the extract chip beside the compass arrow. Show the final rush banner in place of the grey rows, with 24px clearance on all sides.

findings.where: team score panel (210 sp, you 105 sp, p1 105 sp)
findings.what: The panel is semi-transparent over a busy wall. Its edge is blurry and the text is only loosely aligned in it. The big 210 sp and the two small right-hand lines are not baseline-aligned. The label 'team score' is centred while the numbers are not. 'p1' is also inconsistent with 'player 1' and 'you'. The 16px labels are muted grey on a see-through fill, so contrast is weak.
findings.fix: Use a solid --ui-panel fill at 92% opacity or higher with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Put the left-hand column and the right-hand column on shared baselines. Set the sub-lines in tx-1 or tx-2 at 16px with 8px padding. Rename 'p1' to 'player 1' and 'you' to 'player 1' or keep 'you' only if consistent.

findings.what: The two bars are flat saturated fills (blue and green) in a different style from the dark panels used everywhere else. The hp text is much larger than the armour text. The labels sit inside the bar with weak contrast on the blue, and the bars have no panel behind them. The hp bar is cut close to the screen edge, with about 24px of margin against the 5% rule.
findings.fix: Put both bars in one --ui-panel container with a 4px radius and 8px padding. Use 20px labels in the same weight for both rows. Use --ok for hp and a muted blue for armour. Add a dark text track behind the numbers. Pull the container in to a 5% margin.

findings.where: weapon slots 1 to 0 and the ammo panel at bottom right
findings.what: Only the first slot and the selected slot 5 are drawn, and the remaining numbers 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 0 float with no tile, over a busy wall, almost illegible. The selected tile uses a gold/amber border that reads as rarity or warn, not the lime accent. The ammo panel is a different box, with a larger radius and a different border colour than the other HUD boxes. 'support mg' is a muted 20px label that is too faint. The slot counts of 360 are tiny.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 56px tiles with --ui-panel fill and a --ui-line border, with the number at 16px. Make the selected tile's border 2px lime (--acc). Use the same 4px radius and border for the ammo panel. Raise the weapon name to tx-1 at 20px. Make the 360 counts 16px or larger.

findings.what: It is styled as a web select, with a light border and a chevron, while the rest of the HUD uses dark flat panels. It is also 4px from the top edge, and its text is a different size from the other HUD text. It breaks the one-style rule, and the HUD is meant to be a vertical 1 by 1 list.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a --ui-panel chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use 20px text. Pull it in to a 24px margin. Match it to the other top-right items (cw-trcol).

findings.where: left cluster: keyboard tag, player 1 bar, 2 minutes left chip
findings.what: The keyboard badge at the top left is cramped against the corner. The 'player 1' name plate has a thin bar that looks like a stray stripe. The '2 minutes left' chip has an orange left bar and a doc icon, so it reads as a different component from the others. The three share no alignment axis, since they sit at x=10, 15 and 20.
findings.fix: Put them on one left margin at x=48 (5%). Use one chip style: --ui-panel, a 1px border, a 4px radius, a 16px label, and warn amber only for a 3px left bar on the time chip. Remove the duplicate 'player 1' name plate above the character, or the one at the left.

findings.where: f1 controls hint and 'in pillager's party' label, bottom centre
findings.what: The two small chips float with no relationship to each other or to the weapon bar. 'in pillager's party' is 14px or smaller on a barely visible dark box. 'f1 controls' is above slot 1 with its edge touching the tile row. A capital letter does not appear, but the apostrophe wording is explaining text and is clutter.
findings.fix: Remove 'in pillager's party' from the raid, or move it to the pause screen. Put 'f1 controls' in the mid-bottom-left spot the owner ordered, at 16px, with the key in a 1px bordered keycap and 16px of clearance from the slot row.

findings.what: The red box is a good call to action, but its warning triangle, the 32px title and the 'kills x1.05 sp' line are all in different weights, and the red left edge plus the red bottom bar give it a double border. The 'x1.05 sp' string is awkward, and 'sp' is used as a multiplier unit.
findings.fix: Use one 3px --danger bar on the left only. Put the title at 32px f-cond 700. Reword the second line as 'kills score x1.05' at 16px tx-2.

v.verdict: The final rush banner is now a wide red-edged panel, but the top-centre stack is still a pile of overlapping boxes, the HUD uses inconsistent type sizes, and the bottom-left and bottom-right clusters are untouched.

findings.what: The banner is 620px wide but holds only a title and a short subline, so more than half of it is empty black. It sits flush under the team score box with no gap, and the faded 'the seal 0%' text bleeds through its top edge. The red left bar is only 4px and the bottom red line is a half-width stub, so the banner reads as unfinished. The title is lime-free red but only about 32px, with a 20px subline.
findings.fix: Shrink the banner to about 420px wide with 16px padding. Centre it on x=960 and put it at y=260 with 24px of clear space above and below. Fill it with --ui-panel at 90% opacity. Use a 4px --danger left bar and drop the partial bottom line. Set the title to 32px --danger and the subline to 20px tx-2. Remove the 'the seal' text from behind it.

findings.where: top-centre stack (extract chip, timer, weather icon, team score)
findings.what: Four unrelated boxes sit at different heights with different widths. The timer (x887-1033) and the team score box (x807-1113) have different widths, so they are not centred on a shared axis. The extract chip, timer and weather icon are jammed together with 0 to 8px gaps. The team score box mixes 16px labels with 20px bold numbers, and the 'you' and 'p2' rows are indented unevenly.
findings.fix: Use one 16px gap between all boxes and centre each on x=960. Make the timer the only 56px hero. Put the extract chip on the left of the timer at the same top edge and the weather icon on the right. Make the team score box the same width as the timer row. Show 'team score' as a 16px tx-2 label above one 20px row, with 'you' and 'p2' left-aligned at 16px tx-2.

findings.where: bottom-left bars (armour 60, hp 100) and f1 controls chip
findings.what: The armour and hp bars use different type sizes, about 20px and 32px. The hp bar sits 8px from the screen bottom and the armour bar sits on the busy wall texture. The bars' labels have no plate behind them and the f1 controls chip floats at x410 over the world.
findings.fix: Use one 16px label and one 20px value format for both bars. Make both bars 32px high and 400px wide, stacked with an 8px gap and left edge at x=48. Put each label on a dark --ui-panel plate. Set the f1 chip's left edge at x=48 on its own row 16px above the bars.

findings.what: The panel is 10px from the right edge, outside the 5% margin, and it is much heavier than the rest of the HUD. The weapon name is 28px and the count is about 70px, which is bigger than the 56px hero cap. The weapon slots sit on a separate strip 400px to the left, so ammo and weapon switching read as two unrelated groups.
findings.fix: Inset the panel 48px from the right and bottom edges. Cap the ammo count at 56px f-cond 800 and the weapon name at 20px. Move the weapon slot tiles to sit directly left of the ammo panel on the same baseline.

findings.where: weapon slots 1-0 on the bottom strip
findings.what: Only slots 4 and 6 have tiles. The other digits are bare 14px numerals floating on the wall texture at about 30% contrast, so they are nearly unreadable and look like debris. The lime border on slot 6 is the only focus cue and it is fairly thin.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as equal 64px tiles with a --ui-line border and --ui-panel fill. Put the number in a 16px label inside each tile. Dim empty tiles to 40% opacity. Give the selected tile a 3px --acc border.

findings.what: The goals panel is a 300px bar with a chevron, but it has no label and its text is about 24px, a size that is not on the type scale. It sits 20px from the right edge and 22px from the top, so it does not line up with the 48px margin. It looks different from the timer box with its own corner radius and fill.
findings.fix: Set the text at 20px f-cond 600 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Inset it 48px from the right edge and 24px from the top, and match its height to the timer box.

findings.where: player 2 tags (left bar at x15-170, y323-358 and world label at x990-1050, y858-875)
findings.what: The player 2 bar on the left is a cyan-tinted strip with a thin teal underline and no value, so it reads as a stray label. The world tag has about 12px text on a thin cyan plate and is hard to read over the busy ground.
findings.fix: Make the left player 2 tag a 16px label on a --ui-panel plate with a 4px cyan bar and a 100% value readout. Raise the world tag to 16px on a --ui-panel plate with 4px padding. Keep player 2 cyan.

findings.what: The chip is jammed into the corner, 5px from the top-left, with a 14px label and a thin outline. It is the only element on the left side of the top edge and it breaks the 48px margin.
findings.fix: Inset it to x=48, y=24. Use a 16px label on --ui-panel with a 4px radius, or drop it once the input device is already shown by the f1 prompt.

v.verdict: The top-centre is now a clear timer-then-banner hierarchy with consistent dark panels, but the final rush banner is oversized and mostly empty, the team score box has uneven alignment, and the bottom-left bars still sit loose on the map.

findings.what: The banner is 620x125px and about 60% empty on the right. It sits over the playfield and hides the centre of the map. It also competes with the 1:30 timer, because the red title is the first thing the eye lands on.
findings.fix: Shrink it to fit its content, about 320x72px, with 16px padding. Keep the 4px red left bar, put the warning glyph and 'final rush' on one line at 20-24px, and put 'kills x1.05 sp' at 16px in tx-2. Anchor it 16px under the team score panel.

findings.where: team score panel, below the timer
findings.what: The 'team score' label is centred over the 210 sp number, while the 'you / p1' column is right-aligned and sits on different baselines. The panel is 306px wide, wider than the 146px timer above it. The 'p1' label is ambiguous next to 'you'. Both pieces of text are small, about 16px.
findings.fix: Make the panel the same width as the timer, or 220px. Use a two-column grid with a shared baseline: 210 sp at 32px tx-1 on the left, and 'you 105' and 'player 2 105' at 16px on the right. Use 8px padding and a 1px --ui-line-hi border with a 4px radius.

findings.what: The two bars have different heights (about 20px and 32px) and different type sizes ('armour 60' at about 20px, 'hp 100' at about 32px). Their left edges sit at 24px and don't line up with the 'f1 controls' chip above them. The text sits directly on the saturated bar fills. There is no shared container, so they read as two unrelated widgets.
findings.fix: Put both in one --ui-panel container with a 4px radius and 8px padding. Make both bars 20px tall with 20px f-cond 600 labels. Use --ok for hp. Right-align the numbers on a dark track. Align the container left edge with the weapon slots at a 5% margin.

findings.what: The empty slots (2, 3, 5 to 0) are bare numbers that disappear into the map. Only slots 1 and 4 have tiles. The selected slot has a thin amber/gold outline, not lime --acc. The ammo counts '144' inside the tiles are tiny. The slots don't line up with the ammo panel at right, which sits 8px lower than the bottom edge of the slot row.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 56px tiles with --ui-panel at 85% fill and a 1px --ui-line border. Keep the numbers at 16px in tx-2. Make the selected tile's border 2px --acc lime, and set ammo counts at 16px tx-1. Align the bottoms of the slot row and the ammo panel.

findings.what: The panel is larger than the top-centre elements, with four lines at mixed sizes and a 24px inset. Its third-level lines are indented by different amounts, and 'run goals' repeats what the title already says. The chevron is tiny. It is a lot of text for a quiet corner and reads as clutter next to the final rush banner.
findings.fix: Drop the 'run goals' line, and align the three goal rows to one left edge at 16px. Right-align the '+400 sp' rewards in tx-2. Collapse the panel to just 'goals 0/3' by default and open it with a key. Set the panel inset to 24px to match the HUD margin.

findings.what: The 'keyboard' chip has a different fill and border from every other panel, and sits at a 10px inset. The 'player 1' tag is blue with a teal bar and is clipped by the screen edge at x=0. Player 1 should be amber by the guide, not blue.
findings.fix: Restyle the chip as a --ui-panel at 16px with a 4px radius and 24px inset. Move the 'player 1' tag inside the safe margin and colour it amber for P1 as the guide says.

findings.what: The chip floats between the bars and the map, with a lighter fill than the other panels. At 16px with low contrast, it competes with the armour bar. It touches the top edge of the wall art.
findings.fix: Use the standard --ui-panel fill, put the chip 16px above the bars container, and use tx-2 text at 16px. Align its left edge with the bars container.

v.verdict: A small, empty 'tonight's best' card sits dead-centre over a busy blurred lobby: it is tidy and on-style, but there is almost nothing in it and the empty state reads as a placeholder.

findings.what: The empty state is a 20px line in a 560x255 card, with about 80px of dead space around it. The card has no content hierarchy and looks unfinished. 'no scores yet' is the same size and weight as the title's neighbours, so nothing carries the screen.
findings.fix: Either skip the card when no scores exist, or fill the empty state: a --tx-2 line at 20px f-body 400 and a 56px hero '0 sp' above it, or a dim row skeleton of 3 ranks. Shrink the card height to about 200px.

findings.where: 'press any key' prompt, bottom right of card (1074-1206, 617)
findings.what: The prompt is the primary action on this walk-up screen, but it is tucked into the card's lower-right corner at about 22px. A lime ring dot plus white text give two competing accents and the dot looks like a radio button, so it reads as a selectable option. There is also a competing x button in the top-right.
findings.fix: Centre the prompt on the card's bottom edge at 24px f-cond 700 with the key name in lime (--acc) and tx-1 for the rest. Drop the ring dot or make it a 16px key cap. Drop the x, because any key already closes the card.

findings.what: The scrim is weak, about 45% in places. The blurred lobby (neon circles, characters, 'player 2' label in amber and the 'keyboard' pill at top) stays loud and fights the card. The 'player 2' label is legible and bright, so it draws the eye away from the card.
findings.fix: Raise the scrim to rgba(6,7,8,.80) per --scrim and hide the world-space labels ('player 2', 'keyboard') while a modal is open.

findings.where: card header, title 'tonight's best' and x button
findings.what: The title is about 30px and fine. The x is a 48px boxed button with a hairline border and a tiny 12px glyph, which is weak against the card. The lime 36px tab on the top edge is a lone accent with no meaning (not focus, not selected).
findings.fix: Make the x glyph 20px with a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 40px square, aligned to the title's baseline row. Either extend the lime top bar across the full card width at 2px as a deliberate header rule, or remove it.

findings.what: The card has a 1px border and a divider at y=571 that separates nothing meaningful (one empty line above, the prompt below). Padding is uneven: 32px left, but 14px above the title against 28px below the divider.
findings.fix: Use 32px padding on all sides (--sp-4), remove the divider or apply it only above a footer, and set the title row at 56px high.

findings.what: The wordmark is a small, plain 28px white word at the top left, cut by the left letterbox bar. It sits on a busy backdrop with no relationship to the card, and it is not a logo.
findings.fix: Either use the real logo art at about 40px height with a 5% margin (96px), or remove it while the modal is up.

findings.what: The card is a generic dark rectangle with a hairline border. Nothing says extraction shooter (no rank rows, no sp, no crest), and the screen has no sense of occasion for a leaderboard.
findings.fix: Give the card the same header treatment as the other windows (title, then a lime 2px rule). Show the sp column header and rank numerals in f-cond 800, even when empty, so the structure is visible.

v.verdict: The card is clean and on-palette, but it is a tiny, empty, dull modal that sits in the middle of a busy lobby that is barely dimmed, so it carries no hierarchy and no identity.

findings.what: The card is mostly empty. "no scores yet" is a small plain line with no icon or structure, and the card has no table, rank column or hero number to show what a filled board would look like. It reads as a placeholder, not a designed screen.
findings.fix: Design the empty state as a 3-row ghost table (rank, name, sp) at 20px in tx-2 over --ui-line dividers, or put the one hero line at 56px/800. Drop the card to a fixed 560x360 so it matches the other windows.

findings.what: The backdrop is blurred but still bright and busy. The lobby characters, coloured rings and the "player 2" label stay visible and compete with the card, so the eye keeps leaving the title. The scrim looks lighter than the guide's .80.
findings.fix: Set the scrim to rgba(6,7,8,.80) plus the blur, and hide the lobby labels while the card is open ("player 2" at ~y=758 and the "keyboard" tag at the top).

findings.what: The card is about 557x255 px, roughly 29% of the screen width. The guide says windows are a centred card taking up about 90 percent of the screen (his Q43), so this is out of step with the shop, codex and the other windows.
findings.fix: Use the same 90% card shell as the other windows, with the 56px header and 72px footer rows. Or, if this is meant as a small dialog, say so in the guide.

findings.where: "press any key" prompt, bottom-right of card
findings.what: The prompt is the right action, and its lime ring dot has good contrast. But it is right-aligned at 20px with a hollow radio-style glyph, which looks like a selectable option rather than a key prompt. It also sits next to an x close button, so there are two dismiss affordances.
findings.fix: Centre the prompt in a 72px footer row. Replace the radio glyph with a key cap showing the device's key or button. Keep the x only if the x is a click target for mouse users.

findings.where: title "tonight's best" and the lime tick above the card
findings.what: The title is 32px, which is correct, but the lime tick at the top-left of the card (about 36x3 px) is the only accent in the card and looks like a rendering artefact. The title and the prompt also both take lime or white weight, so the boldness is split between the two.
findings.fix: Make the tick a full-width 3px lime top bar, or remove it. Keep the title as the single bold element and set the prompt to 16px tx-2 with only the key cap in lime.

findings.what: The body text is about 18px, which is not one of the five sizes. The divider line is faint, the gaps (title to body 60px, body to divider 36px, divider to prompt 45px) are uneven and off the 8px grid, and the left padding of 32px does not match the 24px top padding.
findings.fix: Set the text to 20px tx-2. Use 24px gaps between every block and 32px padding on all four sides. Make the divider --ui-line-hi.

findings.what: The button is 48x46 px, which is nearly square but not exactly, and its border and glyph are tiny at 1080 on a couch. The pad focus state is not shown, so it is unclear whether it takes focus.
findings.fix: Make it 48x48 with a 2px --ui-line-hi border, a 24px x glyph, and a lime focus ring when focused.

findings.what: The wordmark is small, floats over a bright, blurred part of the backdrop with no panel, and is the only chrome on the screen. It does not tie to the card and adds no identity. It also sits close to the 5% margin guide, at x=96, and is a bold white condensed type with no logo treatment.
findings.fix: Dim it to tx-2 at 20px, or remove it while the modal is open. If it stays, put it on the same baseline grid as the card title.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is legible and mostly lower case, but its top-centre cluster is crowded, it uses too many type sizes and colours, and the world labels and floating tags are untidy.

findings.where: top-centre cluster (clock, team score, extract 49m, packing floor)
findings.what: Four stacked elements sit in one column. The clock, the score card and the extract pill have different widths and fills, and the 'packing floor' zone label is letter-spaced and collides with the wall edge at x≈1065. The score card shows 'team score', '0 sp', 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' as four competing text sizes. The 'you' and 'p1' lines are redundant, and 'p1' is the same player.
findings.fix: Merge the clock and score into one 8px-grid panel with the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius. Show 'team 0 sp' at 56px hero or 32px, and drop the per-player lines or show them in a single 16px row. Move the zone label to a 16px --tx-2 label with no letter-spacing, 24px below the pill, away from walls.

findings.what: The hp and armour bars have different glyph sizes: 'hp 100' is about 32px while 'armour 60' is about 20px. The bars are bright flat green and blue with no panel behind them, so they read as pasted over the map. 'f1 controls' floats at x≈410–535, unaligned with the bars (x≈25) or the weapon slots, and the controls hint sits directly above the armour bar.
findings.fix: Put both bars in one --ui-panel plate at 24px margin. Use the same 20px f-cond 600 label on both, with a 16px bar height and an 8px gap. Left-align 'f1 controls' to the bar edge at 16px, or fold it into the left-bottom feed.

findings.where: weapon slot bar (1–0) and ammo card
findings.what: The slot bar is hard to read. Slots 3–0 are faint ghost icons with 14px numbers at low contrast. Slot 2's amber selection frame reads as player 1's colour, and lime is meant for 'selected'. The ammo card (30 / 180) is a different panel size, with 'compact smg' at about 28px and 'f' badges on slot 1 that mean nothing. The 180 count under each slot is tiny at about 16px.
findings.fix: Draw the selected slot with a 2px --acc border (lime) and --acc-ink for the number. Raise the inactive numbers to --tx-2 at 16px with at least 4.5:1 contrast. Remove the 'f' badge or label it. Match the ammo card's fill and radius to the other panels, with the weapon name at 20px and 30 at 56px hero.

findings.where: world labels (the long dock cache, elite cache, extraction c available, player 1, xx_beefstuffer69_xx)
findings.what: The label styles are inconsistent. The caches are lilac with a heavy outline and about 24px, the extraction tag is a teal chip, the player 1 tag is a blue chip, and the enemy name is a red-on-dark chip with a stray red '!' above it. The 'in pillager's party' tooltip is a black box with 14px body text floating at the bottom centre with no clear owner. Every label is a different size and shape.
findings.fix: Use one chip spec, with 16px f-cond 600, 4px radius, a --ui-panel fill at 80% and a 3px colour bar for the role (rarity, extract teal, player amber or cyan, danger red). Put the party tooltip on the 16px grid, anchored to the player.

findings.what: The card is tiny and floats in the corner with a thin bar. It uses blue text, while the guide says P1 is amber, and it duplicates the 'player 1' tag above the character in the world.
findings.fix: Use P1 amber for the text or colour bar, and make the type 20px. Remove the duplicate, or fold the card into the bottom-left hp plate.

findings.what: The badge is a small lime-outlined chip tucked against the corner at x=0, with no margin. It is clipped to the screen edge and its green is not the --acc lime.
findings.fix: Inset it 24px and use the standard 16px chip. Colour it --tx-2, since it is not an action.

findings.what: The sun is a small round icon with a dark ring that sits loose next to the clock and does not align with the clock plate's vertical centre or share its fill.
findings.fix: Put it inside the clock panel as a 24px glyph with 8px padding, or remove it.

v.verdict: The easy-mode prompt is a flat, template-looking dialog with a weak hierarchy and a lot of empty space. It sits over a cluttered HUD that has several small craft problems.

findings.where: easy mode dialog, whole card (x492-1427, y260-580)
findings.what: The card has no border, no close or back affordance and no shadow, so it merges into the dark map. The title sits at the top-left with a large empty band under it. The countdown '12' is a tiny grey number at the far right with no label or ring, so a player will not realise it is a timer that auto-resolves. The card is wider than its content needs and feels like a generic template.
findings.fix: Shrink the card to about 720x280 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Add a --scrim .80 layer behind it. Draw the countdown as a 40px ring or bar in --acc around or under the title, and leave no unexplained bare numeral.

findings.what: The lime 'yes' fill is huge (406x100) and the 20px text on it is small by comparison, so the button shouts while its label whispers. 'no' is a thin-outlined box whose border is barely visible at --ui-line, and it has no clear focus state. Both keycap hints ('y', 'n') are plain inline text, not keycaps. The default action is also 'yes' to easy mode, which is an odd pick for a shooter.
findings.fix: Reduce both buttons to 64px tall and set the label to 24px f-cond 700. Give 'no' a 2px --ui-line-hi border and --tx-1 text. Render 'y' and 'n' as 24px keycap chips with a 1px border. Keep lime on only the focused button, and move the focus ring to 'no' if it should be the default.

findings.where: top-centre HUD stack (timer, team score, extract)
findings.what: Three stacked boxes in different widths and styles (the timer card, the team score card, the extract teal pill) crowd the top centre and sit partly under the dialog; the extract pill touches the dialog edge at y 260. The score card holds four text sizes and 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' is cramped. The 10:00 timer is the hero but competes with the lime button.
findings.fix: Merge them into one panel with 8px row padding and a 16px gap to the dialog. Use one 56px hero for the timer and 16px labels for the rest. Drop the duplicate score line, or move it into the left feed.

findings.what: The bars are stacked at different widths and vertical offsets, so the armour bar sits on the sand wall with a light-blue fill and low-contrast white text. The hp bar's 28px text is bigger than any label, and its bar nearly touches the bottom edge (about 24px). Armour and hp fill colours are saturated and don't match the style tokens.
findings.fix: Align the two bars to the same 24px left and bottom margins, 8px apart, both 16px high with 16px labels on a --ui-panel backing. Use --ok for hp and a muted blue for armour, with --tx-1 text on a dark plate.

findings.what: The slots are unevenly spaced and the empty slots 5-0 show only faint numerals on the wall, which look like stray text. The selected slot has an amber border, which clashes with lime meaning 'selected'. Slot 4 carries a small 'f' badge that is unexplained. The ammo card has '25 / 150' in two sizes with 'auto rifle' in grey at about 3:1 contrast.
findings.fix: Draw all ten slots as 88px tiles on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line border. Show the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Raise 'auto rifle' to --tx-2 at 16px on the card. Put the ammo card's right and bottom margins at 24px, matching the left.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' chip and 'in pillager's party' tooltip
findings.what: These float with no alignment to anything. The f1 chip is 14px text on a translucent dark box over the wall, with low contrast. The 'in pillager's party' label is 14px and sits over the player with no panel border. The top-left 'keyboard' chip uses a different style again (green-tinted border, mono-looking).
findings.fix: Use one chip style (--ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px label) for all three. Place 'f1 controls' on the 24px left margin at the same baseline as the hp bar, and drop the 14px tooltip or raise it to 16px.

findings.what: The goals dropdown has a different radius, border and chevron style from the other HUD cards. Its 22px text is a different size again, and it sits tight to the top-right edge at about 18px. It is the only collapsible and looks pasted in.
findings.fix: Use the shared 4px radius, 24px edge margin, 20px text and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Match its height to the timer card (about 72px).

v.verdict: The shot is now a busy in-raid HUD instead of the 'tonight's best' card, and it has too many competing panels and a heavy always-open controls list. Only the ammo hero number and the weapon slots have clear hierarchy.

findings.what: A 310x345px keys panel is open over the play area, with about 25 rows at roughly 14-16px. It is the biggest block on screen and competes with the action. The raid spec calls for a one-line fold at mid-bottom left, opened with F1.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single 16px line ('f1 controls') at mid-bottom left. If the party demo must keep the full list, shrink it to about 220px wide and give it a 60% opacity fill. Hide the 'full list' footer row.

findings.what: Seven rows of 14-16px text, with dead players in dim tx-2 grey and '$3,950 dead' columns that are hard to read at couch distance. The header says 'current pillagers 0' and the footer says '0 out - 3 dead', so the same information appears twice. The panel has no clear title and its border does not match the controls panel.
findings.fix: Keep only the title and 'you $1,647' at 20px, and fold the dead rows behind the chevron. Raise the dead-row text to 16px at the tx-2 floor of 4.5:1. Remove the '0 out - 3 dead' footer. Use the same 4px radius and 1px --ui-line-hi border as the other panels.

findings.where: extract markers, top-centre 'extract 134m' and right edge 'c 134m'
findings.what: Extract distance is drawn twice, in two teal pills with different sizes and styles. This breaks the one-place-per-line rule and splits the eye between two points.
findings.fix: Keep the top-centre banner at 20px f-cond 700. Turn the edge marker into a 16px arrow only, with no repeated text.

findings.what: The red and green circle icons, 'crashing through' in red and 'in cover' in green are five separate chips in different colours. The 'hp 100' number sits over the bar and its text runs into the bottom edge at 1068, which is inside the 5% margin. Red text on the dark panel also puts danger colour on a status that is not a danger.
findings.fix: Move the hp block up to y=1000 or higher so the 54px bottom margin holds. Put 'hp' at 16px and '100' at 32px above a 12px bar. Merge the status chips into one 16px tx-1 row with small icons, and keep red for real damage.

findings.where: world labels: 'the long dock cache' (purple, 1648-1818 x 180), 'xx_beefstuffer69_xx' tag, 'pillager' tags
findings.what: There are four different label styles: a purple glow, a red filled tag, a blue-grey tag and the top-left 'pillager' bar. The purple label is off-palette. The orphan 'pillager' health bar at 14-170 x 325-358 has no panel context.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style: 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 on a --scrim pill at 4px radius. Use rarity or accent colour only for hostile (--danger) and player (amber P1 or cyan P2). Fold the 'pillager' bar into the hp block at bottom-left.

findings.where: weapon bar, 553-1010 x 955-1058, with ghost slots 3, 5-8 and 0
findings.what: The weapon slots are the clearest element, but the ghost slot numbers are about 14px at very low contrast and the ghost weapon silhouettes add noise. The slot 4 ammo bar in amber looks the same as the selected slot 1 border.
findings.fix: Remove the ghost silhouettes and keep only the three filled slots, or draw empty slots at a uniform 40% opacity with 16px numbers. Reserve the lime border for the selected slot only, and use tx-2 for the ammo bar.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' dropdown, 1603-1901 x 18-54, and the 'keyboard' chip, top-left
findings.what: The dropdown is a wide black bar with a chevron and no visible content. It looks like a closed web select. The 'keyboard' chip in the corner is a debug-looking label. The two use different fills and borders.
findings.fix: Collapse 'run info' to a 160px chip or hide it until pressed. Remove the 'keyboard' chip, or show it only for the first 5 seconds.

findings.what: The block works as the hero (12 / 24 at 56px), but its right padding is about 16px against 8px at the screen edge, and 'b / i backpack' at 14px is hard to read. The 'scav pistol' title has no weight contrast against the number.
findings.fix: Inset the block 48px from the right and bottom edges. Raise the hint to 16px at the tx-2 floor. Make '12' tx-1 800, '/ 24' tx-2 600, and the title 20px tx-2.

v.verdict: The picture is now a busy in-raid HUD rather than the earlier night card. The raid controls list sits open on screen, and several elements repeat or break the palette, so it reads as a dense debug overlay with no clear first read.

findings.what: The controls list is fully open, about 310x345px, and sits mid-left. The settled rule says a career raid shows one folded short line, mid-bottom left, and F1 opens it. The open list covers the play area and is the biggest block on screen.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line ('f1 controls') anchored bottom-left at x=48, above the hp bar. Open it only on F1. If the screen is a party-demo walk-up, hide the list after about 8s.

findings.where: top-centre 'extract 134m' pill and right-edge 'c 134m' arrow chip
findings.what: The extract distance is drawn twice, at (960,60) and (1825,493). This breaks the 'every line shows in ONE place' rule. The two chips also differ in size and weight.
findings.fix: Keep the top-centre banner. Make the edge marker a 24px teal arrow with no text, or remove it.

findings.where: top-left stack: 'keyboard' tag, 'current pillagers' panel, 'pillager' bar
findings.what: Three unrelated boxes with different borders, fills and text sizes (about 14-16px) are stacked along the left edge. The value-at-risk table has a chevron, five rows of dim grey text and a footer ('0 out · 3 dead'). The 'pillager' name appears again as a floating tag over the player's head. The result is clutter, and the muted grey rows fall under the 4.5:1 floor.
findings.fix: Collapse the table to a single row ('value at risk $1,647'), expanded on a key. Drop the 'pillager' bar label, since hp already sits bottom-left. Use one panel style: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Raise the dim rows to --tx-2 at 16px or more.

findings.what: This is a magenta/lilac text label in a colour that is not in the palette. It floats loose with no panel. It is also loud, and nothing at that size and colour has any other job in the HUD.
findings.fix: Set it in --tx-1 at 20px f-cond 600, with a 1px --ui-line underline or a small panel, or show it as a short banner. Do not use a violet that looks like the elite rarity colour.

findings.where: hierarchy: bottom-right ammo card vs bottom-left hp bar and top clock
findings.what: The hero ammo number is correct at about 56px, but the hp bar is a wide solid green block with 'hp 100' in white, and it competes with the ammo number. The clock '15:00' and the lime-highlighted weapon slot add more bright points. The eye lands on the hp bar before the ammo, and nothing leads from one to the next.
findings.fix: Shrink the hp bar to 320x16px with a 20px 'hp 100' label above it. Keep the ammo number as the one 56px/800 element. Reserve lime/amber for the selected slot only.

findings.what: The inactive slots 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 0 show faint ghost silhouettes, and their numerals are about 14px in grey. This reads as noise and sits below the readability floor. The pale 'f' badge on slot 2 is different again.
findings.fix: Show only the owned slots (1, 2, 4). Draw empty slots as 1px --ui-line outlines with no silhouette. Set the numerals at 16px in --tx-2.

findings.where: status pills 'crashing through' and 'in cover', bottom-left
findings.what: Two pills sit side by side with different styles: a red outline with red text at about 24px, and a teal-green outline at 20px. Two round glyph buttons sit next to them. Four different shapes are crowded into one 370px strip, and danger red is used for a neutral status.
